title_en: The women of Madyan and their father
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: A man who came to the water of Madyan found there a crowd of people watering, and found apart from them a pair of women holding back, and when he asked what their concern was, they said that they could not water until the shepherds withdrew, since their father was a very old man.
He watered for them, then went back to the shade and said, my Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.

One of them came to him with modesty and said that her father was calling him to repay him for watering for them, and when he came to her father and told him his account, the father said, do not fear, you have escaped from the wrongdoing people.
One of them said to her father that he should hire him, since the best one to hire is the strong and the trustworthy.

The father said that he wished to marry one of these daughters of his to him on condition that he work for him for eight years, and if he completed ten it would be of his own accord, adding that he did not wish to burden him and that he would find him, if God willed, among the righteous.
The man answered that this was agreed between them, that whichever term he completed there would be no wrong against him, and that God was a guardian over what they said.

chapters.summary_md: A man came to the water of Madyan and watered for a pair of women who were holding back [c1][c2]. Their father called him, and one of the women said that he should be hired as the strong and trustworthy one [c3][c4]. The father proposed that he work for him for eight years, or ten if he chose, and offered one of his daughters in marriage [c5].
chapters.body_md: A man who came to the water of Madyan found there a crowd of people watering, and found apart from them a pair of women holding back, and when he asked what their concern was, they said that they could not water until the shepherds withdrew, since their father was a very old man [c1]. He watered for them, then went back to the shade and said, my Lord, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me [c2]. One of them came to him with modesty and said that her father was calling him to repay him for watering for them, and when he came to her father and told him his account, the father said, do not fear, you have escaped from the wrongdoing people [c3]. One of them said to her father that he should hire him, since the best one to hire is the strong and the trustworthy [c4]. The father said that he wished to marry one of these daughters of his to him on condition that he work for him for eight years, and if he completed ten it would be of his own accord, adding that he did not wish to burden him and that he would find him, if God willed, among the righteous [c5]. The man answered that this was agreed between them, that whichever term he completed there would be no wrong against him, and that God was a guardian over what they said [c6].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat name neither the women, their father nor the man [c1]. They record the terms the father offered, eight years with ten as a favour from the man [c5].
chapters.kids_md: A man came to the water of Madyan [c1]. He saw a pair of women holding back and watered for them [c1][c2]. Their father asked to see him, and one of the women said that he was strong and trustworthy [c3][c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that after helping the women the man turned to God and said that he needed whatever good God might send [c2]. Another is that one of the women described the best person to hire as strong and trustworthy [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the names of the women, their father or the man, or where Madyan lay.
- Not established: the Arabic word in the ayah that is rendered years can also mean pilgrimages, and years is the usual reading.
- Not established: which of the women the father meant, or whether the marriage took place within these ayat; the ayah records the offer and the man's reply.
- Not established: how long the man stayed, or how long the work lasted.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the father is identified with a prophet of Madyan, and the women and their father are given names in later works.
The man in these ayat is not named in them; linking him to a person of the same surah is an inference from the context.
Hadith to add later: reports about the women of Madyan and their father, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
